method: A glyph chain over the whole line (four symbols of context; the word space and the line end are ordinary symbols) that starts afresh at each line. The only thing the writer knows about layout is which kind of line it is starting: the chain's start symbol is one mark for a line that opens a paragraph and another for any other line, as counted on the public paragraph lines. No rule mentions p, f, gallows or any glyph: whatever the first lines carry is what the counts after the paragraph-opening mark hold, fading as the four-symbol context moves on. One table for the whole text, no word list, no copying, no drift. Fitted on the public training pages only (certain paragraph lines); lines containing a four-word run of the manuscript are redrawn. 'lines' are lines written with the ordinary start mark, 'first_lines' lines written with the paragraph-opening mark; the scorer lays first_lines on the lines that open a paragraph. Local robustness on the practice split (real 15.4, threshold 3): seeds 1, 2, 3 give 8.1, 7.1, 8.9; fitted on every other public page only, 7.3 (even) and 8.6 (odd). The same text also reproduces F-003 (58.0), which here is not written in by hand as in R-003. Limit of this attack, measured on the synthetic text: the excess sits almost wholly in the first word. p or f opens 53% of first words of first_lines (public pages 51%) but only 0.9% of their later words against 0.6% on other lines, where the public pages have 2.6% against 0.25%. The chain forgets the opening mark after four symbols, so it passes F-008 through the first word that F-008 shares with F-003; the roughly tenfold excess of p and f later on first lines is not reproduced and would need its own fact (first lines with their first word set aside).
